intended_object: The affine span (affine hull) of a set of points s in an affine space P over a ring k: the smallest affine subspace containing s. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
I read the body and the two definitions it relies on. The carrier is `spanPoints k s`, defined as `{p | ∃ p₁ ∈ s, ∃ v ∈ vectorSpan k s, p = v +ᵥ p₁}`. Here `vectorSpan k s` is `Submodule.span k (s -ᵥ s)`, the span of all differences of points of s.

- **Empty set:** the carrier is empty, which is the correct affine span of ∅.
- **Nonempty set:** the carrier is p₁ + span(s − s) for any p₁ in s. This is the standard description of the affine hull.

The closure proof is sound: if p₁ and p₂ lie in the set, then p₁ − p₂ lies in the vector span, so c•(p₁ − p₂) + p₃ stays in `spanPoints`. That makes it an affine subspace, and every affine subspace containing s must contain all of these points, so it is the smallest one.

The generality is right. It works for any ring k, any module V and any affine space P, which matches Mathlib's general `AffineSubspace` framework. This is itself Mathlib's own definition of the notion (line 518 of `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/AffineSubspace/Defs.lean`), so there is no other Mathlib counterpart to cite.
